newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BELFOX SEEKS SYNERGIES WITH BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BELFOX SEEKS SYNERGIES WITH BOURSE.

text.p: Belgian futures and options exchange Belfox said on Monday one of its objects for 1997 was to look at areas where it could work more closely with the Brussels stock exchange.

"It's about time we tried to develop synergies - (though) it's only possible if these can bring advantages for the two parties and the market as a whole," said Jos Schmitt, president of the Belfox management committee.
One of the easiest areas to start with was marketing, and Belfox and the stock exchange were already taking steps in that direction, he said.

Schmitt was speaking after the presentation of Belfox's annual results. Belfox, started five years ago, announced revenue of 279 million Belgian francs for 1996, a rise of 11 percent from 1995. Net income rose 80 percent to 93 million francs.

Asked about the possibility of an eventual merger between Belfox and the Brussels stock exchange, which has been undergoing a far-reaching modernisation programme for months, Schmitt said now was not the right time for such a step.
"Before you start talking about that, they have to get through all their restructuring. You could reconsider (the question of a merger) then," he said.
"But that doesn't mean you can't work (together) in functional areas, such as information technology, in the mean time," he added.
Gradually merging their activities, leaving Belfox and the stock exchange as holding companies, would be a more pragmatic approach than a straightforward merger, he said.
